## labs/nvidia/vk-gaussian-splatting

Vulkan Gaussian Splatting viewer - Renders Gaussian Splat and 3DGRT particle scenes natively over Vulkan.

Status: opt-in. Install: git-clone. Artifact: viewer. Arm64: unknown. GB10: unverified. Comfy shape: viewer.
Input: a particle scene file
Output: a rendered view of the scene
Licenses: code NVIDIA sample-code license (SPDX headers). Weights none. Commercial use conditional.
Footprint: 8 GB VRAM, 3 GB disk. Weights: none.
Artifact ref: https://github.com/nvpro-samples/vk_gaussian_splatting.git
Upstream: https://github.com/nvpro-samples/vk_gaussian_splatting
Also: https://github.com/nvpro-samples/vk_wsi
Sources: https://github.com/nvpro-samples/vk_gaussian_splatting

Nothing in this graph touches the GPU. The row's work runs outside the Comfy process through the operator CLI, so the App claims no occupancy and stops no heavy job: the one-heavy-job rule is the CLI's to enforce, next to the heavy confirm and the headroom preflight.

Operator verbs (host shell):
  bazelisk run //:manage -- nvidia-lab status
  bazelisk run //:manage -- nvidia-lab plan vk-gaussian-splatting
  bazelisk run //:manage -- nvidia-lab install vk-gaussian-splatting

Canvas:
1. Preflight prints whether this Spark could run the row today - the catalog row, an aarch64 host, the binary that row's install kind needs, and the artifact ref.
2. The verdict card prints the blocking reason and the sentence that would reopen the row.
3. The tier table prints all 18 rows with their status and licenses.

Gate notes: Being Vulkan it sidesteps the CUDA architecture and aarch64 wheel problems that block the rest of the tier, and it is the only viewer here. It renders, it generates nothing, and it needs a Vulkan-capable GB10 driver path. It stays a host-side viewer beside Comfy rather than an image dependency, on the same rule that keeps SuperSplat out of the image.
Reopen: n/a - opt-in as a host viewer.
Verify: bazelisk test //tests:bats_nvidia_lab_test

Occupancy: none - stop nothing GPU. One GB10 job.
